notes: Documentation claim checked: README says syntax-tree `high` edges are 94.2-100% precise with 33-66% recall, measured on Go, TypeScript, Python and Java. Rust is not in that list. Measured here for Rust high edges: 17/20 = 85% lenient, 13/20 = 65% strict. Recall 32/70 = 45.7% is inside the claimed range.
Roughly 24% of all Rust CALLS edges (1136 of 4739) point at a struct/enum or a Cargo dependency rather than a function; the whole low tier is of this kind.

The resolver has effectively three rules for Rust: same file by bare name (3000 edges), same directory by bare name (1410), repository-unique type name (286). Receiver typing produced 43 edges, 19 of them wrong. Imports and written paths (crate::a::b::f) do not influence the result.
No crash, hang or timeout in any command.

notes: Headline: for Scala the tool builds a definition list and nothing else. There is no call graph, no type hierarchy and no usable find_callers / analyze_impact / find_implementations answer. The documented precision 94-100% / recall 33-66% does not apply: measured recall is 0/40 and precision is undefined.
The Scala tags query in this build appears to be inferred rather than hand-written and contains definition patterns only; Rust, by contrast, yields 18,723 references from 102 files.

`repocortex resolve` on a Scala-only repository prints 'References: 0 ... Edges: 0' and exits 0; `index` reports the run as degraded only because of the partial files, not because the language has no references.
Kinds: every def is `function`; object and case object are `function`; trait is `interface`; class, case class and enum are `class`.
No crash, hang or timeout in any command on any of the three Scala projects.
